title: Fine print: the five lines worth finding
description: Nobody reads all the terms. But five specific lines carry most of the surprises — learn to hunt for them and you have read what matters.

body.heading: 1. The total price, and 2. what happens after the offer
paragraphs: First, find the total: not the monthly figure, not the "from" price, but everything you will pay across the whole agreement, including fees. Second, find the post-offer price — what the service costs when the introductory period ends, because that is the price you will actually live with.
Introductory offers are honest about the honeymoon and quiet about the marriage. The line that says what happens in month seven is the line that decides whether the deal is good.

body.heading: 3. Auto-renewal, 4. cancellation, 5. the exit cost
paragraphs: Third, look for auto-renewal: does the agreement continue by itself, and when are you warned? Fourth, find how to cancel — a button in settings is a very different commitment from a phone call during office hours.

Fifth, find the cost of leaving early: exit fees, notice periods, equipment to return. A cheap deal with an expensive exit is a trap with good lighting. Knowing all five lines takes minutes and converts fine print from fog into facts.

body.heading: Keep the evidence
paragraphs: Screenshot or save the offer terms on the day you sign up. Prices and terms change, and your saved copy is the proof of what was promised. It takes ten seconds and settles arguments months later.

The same habit helps with renewals and price rises. When a company writes to say your price is changing, your saved terms show exactly what you agreed to and when — which makes the conversation about leaving much shorter.

takeaway: In any offer, find the total price, the post-offer price, auto-renewal, how to cancel, and the cost of leaving — five lines that carry nearly all the risk.
